Le regole d'oro
Non sbirciare il telefono degli altri.
Non mostrare il tuo schermo a nessuno.
I morti non parlano. Nemmeno con gli occhi.
E nessuno si offende: è solo un gioco. Più o meno.
C'era una volta
C'era una volta, in una città che non dorme mai, una piazza piena di brava gente. La chiamavano la Città.
Ma tra quella brava gente si nascondeva la Famiglia. Pochi, eleganti, armati. Si conoscevano tutti tra loro… e nessuno conosceva loro.

La busta sigillata
A ciascuno di voi toccherà una busta sigillata: dentro c'è chi siete davvero.
Leggetela da soli. Poi chiudetela nel cuore, e non ditela a nessuno.

Quando cala la notte
Quando cala la notte, il telefono passa di mano in mano, come un segreto che scotta.

La Famiglia sceglie chi non vedrà l'alba. Il Commissario fruga negli affari altrui. Il Dottore veglia su qualcuno.
E chi non ha poteri? Recita. Tocca lo schermo con l'aria di chi trama, perché nessuno sospetti di nessuno.
All'alba, la piazza
All'alba la città si sveglia e conta i suoi morti. Chi cade di notte se ne va col suo segreto.
Allora la piazza si riunisce: si accusa, si giura, si mente.

Quando le voci tacciono, si vota: a voce alta, col dito puntato. Chi prende più voti viene condannato, e la sua carta si gira davanti a tutti.
Se i voti sono pari, la piazza si ferma: oggi nessuna condanna.
Come finisce la storia
La storia finisce bene per la Città quando l'ultimo della Famiglia ha lasciato la piazza.
Finisce bene per la Famiglia quando i suoi uomini sono tanti quanti tutti gli altri: da quel momento, la città è loro.
E qualche anima solitaria gioca una partita tutta sua: la sua busta le dirà come si vince.
Le tre leggi della strada
Prima legge: non si sbircia nel telefono degli altri.
Seconda legge: il proprio schermo non si mostra a nessuno.
Terza legge: i morti non parlano. Né con la bocca, né con gli occhi.
E adesso… che la notte cominci.

Two sides
Picture a big city in the forties. Almost everyone is decent folk: the Town.
Some aren't. They're the Family, and tonight they've got work to do.
The mobsters know each other. Honest folk know nobody. That's the problem.
Your card is secret

By day you can say anything you like about who you are. Even lies. Especially lies.
The night
At night the phone passes from hand to hand. Whoever holds it makes a secret move; everyone else looks away.
The Family picks someone to rub out. The Detective investigates, the Doctor saves.
No powers? Tap PASS, with the same poker face as everyone else. Nobody should know who did what.
The day
At dawn you find out who didn't make it. Whoever dies at night takes their role to the grave.
Then you talk: accusations, alibis, funny looks.
Anyone with a day power taps “Use a power”, then their own face, and uses it with the phone in their hands.
Finally, you vote out loud, all together, and one of you taps the condemned on the phone. Their card is turned over. A tie? Nobody hangs today.
Prefer a secret vote? Pick it before the cards: the phone goes round and everyone votes alone.
Who wins
The Town wins when the whole Family is out.
The Family wins when they are as many as everyone else.
A few odd types play for themselves: their card tells them how to win.
The golden rules
Don't peek at anyone else's phone.
Never show your screen to anyone.
Dead men don't talk. Not even with their eyes.
And nobody takes it personally: it's only a game. More or less.
Once upon a time
Once upon a time, in a city that never sleeps, there was a square full of good people. They called it the Town.
But hiding among those good people was the Family. Few, elegant, armed. They all knew each other… and nobody knew them.
Maybe one of them is sitting at this table. Maybe two.
The sealed envelope
Each of you will get a sealed envelope: inside is who you really are.
Read it alone. Then lock it in your heart, and tell no one.
From tomorrow you may say anything you like about yourselves. The truth… or not.
When night falls
When night falls, the phone passes from hand to hand, like a secret too hot to hold.
Whoever holds it makes their move unseen. The others stare at the wall, the ceiling, their own shoes.
The Family chooses who won't see the dawn. The Detective pokes into other people's business. The Doctor watches over someone.
And those with no powers? They act. They tap the screen like schemers, so that nobody suspects anybody.
At dawn, the square
At dawn the city wakes up and counts its dead. Whoever falls at night leaves with their secret.
Then the square gathers: people accuse, swear, lie.
You! Where were you last night?
When the voices fall silent, you vote: out loud, finger pointed. Whoever gets the most votes is condemned, and their card is turned over for all to see.
If the votes are tied, the square stands still: nobody is condemned today.
How the story ends
The story ends well for the Town when the last of the Family has left the square.
It ends well for the Family when its men are as many as everyone else: from that moment, the city is theirs.
And a few lonely souls play a game all their own: their envelope will tell them how to win.
The three laws of the street
First law: you don't peek at anyone else's phone.
Second law: you show your screen to no one.
Third law: the dead don't talk. Not with their mouths, not with their eyes.
And now… let the night begin.

L’enveloppe scellée
Chacun de vous recevra une enveloppe scellée : dedans, il y a qui vous êtes vraiment.
Lisez-la en secret. Puis gardez-la au fond du cœur, et ne la dites à personne.
Dès demain, vous pourrez raconter ce que vous voulez sur vous. La vérité… ou pas.
Quand tombe la nuit
Quand tombe la nuit, le téléphone passe de main en main, comme un secret qui brûle les doigts.

À l’aube, la place
À l’aube, la ville se réveille et compte ses morts. Qui tombe la nuit s’en va avec son secret.

L’histoire finit bien pour la ville quand le dernier de la Famille a quitté la place.

Première loi : on ne regarde pas dans le téléphone des autres.
Deuxième loi : on ne montre son écran à personne.
Troisième loi : les morts ne parlent pas. Ni avec la bouche, ni avec les yeux.
Et maintenant… que la nuit commence.
